items.summary: Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Apple is reducing the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, a significant shift from a company known for integrating the technology into workflows. In October, Apple lowered the cap from $300 to $200 per day, with further cuts planned down to $100 and possibly as low as $25 outside engineering. The move follows concerns about token costs outweighing unclear productivity gains.
items.title: Apple reportedly cutting internal AI spending caps amid token cost concerns

items.summary: Visa announced six global tech hubs at a new Paya Lebar centre, bringing some 1,500 staff working on agentic AI, next-generation payments and trusted commerce. The firm said the technologies will be deployed across its global network. Visa's president for technology Rajat Taneja called it an extraordinary period of commerce innovation driven by AI and digital money.
items.title: Visa Opens Six Tech Hubs in Singapore

items.summary: Australia’s oldest department store, David Jones, collapsed on Nov 5 after almost 200 years in business. McGrathNicol executives were appointed voluntary administrators while FTI Consulting staff became receivers; the chain keeps trading as administrators seek buyers to recapitalise it. Anchorage Capital Partners had bought the retailer in 2023. Receiver Christopher Hill cited rising costs, an outdated footprint and supply-chain challenges, while chief executive Erica Berchtold said the company has a plan to reset for the future.
items.title: David Jones Collapses After Nearly Two Centuries

items.summary: Opinion writer Courtney C. Radsch argues that the Democratic victories in the House, Senate and state offices signal a voter mandate to confront corporate power and what she calls technofascism. She frames tech accountability—AI governance, monopoly break-ups, media plurality—as central to this agenda, pointing to growing state-level limits on AI products as evidence of popular will. Radsch urges the incoming Congress to use hearings, subpoenas and floor control to hold executives accountable, citing reports that Meta interfered in elections in the US and Brazil. She acknowledges legislative constraints like the Senate filibuster and presidential veto but insists oversight should continue regardless.
items.title: New Congress Faces Test on Big Tech Power After Voter Mandate

items.summary: Databricks announces Apache Spark 4.3, which brings stateful processing to its low-latency Real-Time Mode in Structured Streaming. The release claims sub-150 ms P99 end-to-end latency across three representative benchmarks for streaming aggregation, deduplication, and custom stateful operations. These figures are measurements of the tested workloads rather than a guarantee for every pipeline. Spark 4.3 also introduces native concurrent stage scheduling and pipelined shuffles to support continuous data flow between long-running tasks. The version marks the start of a quarterly release cadence instead of one every six months, with Databricks Runtime availability noted separately in its own release notes.
items.title: Apache Spark 4.3 Adds Stateful Real-Time Processing and Faster Releases

items.summary: The organizers of PyTorch Day China 2026 have announced that the call for proposals closes November 10 at 23:59 China Standard Time. The event is scheduled to take place in Beijing on December 12, gathering developers, machine learning engineers, AI researchers, and open source leaders from across China and beyond. Submissions may include session presentations and lightning talks spanning five topic areas covering model training, efficient inference, PyTorch core technologies, physical AI, and ecosystem applications. CFP notifications are set for November 17, with the schedule to follow on November 18.
items.title: PyTorch Day China 2026 Opens Its Call for Proposals

items.summary: Field engineers at Databricks describe a shift toward open-weight models, citing seven pressures: weak unit economics, rapidly changing model rankings since 2023 (top intelligence ranking changed hands 20+ times), guardrails blocking legitimate work after the Hugging Face incident where GLM 5.2 replaced refused frontier analysis, evolving data-retention policies like Anthropic's 30-day minimum, governance visibility demands, harness effects on benchmarks (61.7% vs 48.1% vs 38.4%), and open-weight models now matching frontier performance at lower cost. Databricks' Unity Gateway lets teams switch models via config; average unique models per customer rose from 4.2 to 7.1, with ~40% open-weight across weeks ending January 5 and July 27, 2026. CEO Ali Ghodsi told CNBC the $3 billion July raise partly secures GPU capacity for open models.
items.title: Databricks Pushes Open-Weight Models for Enterprise AI Control

items.summary: On Halloween, Victorian Labor posted an AI-generated campaign video depicting Liberal leader Jess Wilson warning that a future Liberal government would force Australians to pay $150,000 for heart attack care. The claims were drawn from remarks Wilson made at a press conference about a $1.27bn plan to fund public elective surgeries in private hospitals. Premier Ben Carroll defended the video as her own words, but Wilson called it a smear campaign and denied Americanising Victoria's health system. Labor described the video as garbage. Experts including Clancy Moore of Transparency International Australia and Timothy Koskie at the University of Sydney say such deepfakes erode trust and call for truth-in-advertising laws.
items.title: Victorian parties clash over AI election videos of leaders

items.summary: After Democratic candidates won many state and congressional races on Tuesday—including in Texas, a national data center hotspot—some tech industry figures turned to space-based computing. Elon Musk posted that “data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” while others cited companies like Google, SpaceX, Blue Origin, and startups such as Starcloud already pursuing orbital compute. Experts caution that space facilities are costlier than land-based ones and cannot reach hyperscale size. In Texas specifically, a split legislature between Democratic control of the House and Republican control of the Senate may limit immediate change, though advocates expect an interesting legislative season.
items.title: Democratic Wins Push Tech Figures Toward Space Data Centers

items.summary: After Democrats took control of Congress in the November midterm, analysts say anger over data centers has become a political force that may limit where and how they are built. Exit polls showed more than half of respondents believe AI will do more harm than good, while almost 80% oppose building them nearby; nearly 60% called them a major voting factor. States like Ohio passed bans or face delays in Georgia and Texas, and candidates across several states won by opposing the buildout. Nadine Smith of Color of Change framed Tuesday's election as a referendum on who this economy is built for.
items.title: Midterm backlash against data centers could reshape AI buildout

items.summary: Voters in recent elections backed candidates and measures favoring restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. Redbud Consulting reported that 38 of 44 ballot measures restricting data centers passed across 10 states so far. Analysts say most rules affect projects planned for 2028, not those approved through 2027. Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race; Bloomberg reports about 13 gigawatts of capacity is now exposed. Advisors warn permits and reviews will slow construction regardless.
items.title: Big Tech Frames Voter AI Restrictions as Anti-Trump, Not Anti-Tech

items.summary: On Election Day, California voters rejected Proposition 45, a measure backed by the state Chamber of Commerce that would have sped environmental review under CEQA. As of Wednesday afternoon with more than half the ballots counted, just over 54 percent opposed it and about 46 percent supported it; nonpartisan Public Policy Institute polling showed support falling from 73 percent to 46 percent between July and October. No on Prop 45 spokesperson Woody Little said millions voted to defend core environmental protections. Elsewhere, Colorado voters rejected Amendment 82 protecting natural gas sales, while Arizona and Texas measures touched utilities and water fees. The outcome reflected broad voter support for safeguarding the environment amid concerns over housing, energy costs and climate goals.
items.title: California Voters Reject Environmental Law Overhaul

items.summary: On an election day, the Alabama Public Service Commission voted to request that Alabama Power voluntarily stop billing customers for advertising costs immediately, rather than waiting until a new law takes effect in 2029. The utility spends more than $6 million annually on general advertising, roughly $4 per customer according to federal filings. President Cynthia Lee Almond moved the measure; commissioners Jeremy Oden and Chris Beeker IV voted yes. Energy Alabama's Daniel Tait praised the action as strong customer protection. Alabama Power did not respond to a request for comment. The vote comes amid criticism of rising electricity prices ahead of a commission overhaul in January.
items.title: Alabama Regulators Seek Immediate End to Utility Advertising Fees

items.summary: Electrek reviews BLUETTI's new Apex 200 portable power station, launching November 4 with standalone early-bird pricing starting at $1,099 through November 18. The unit offers 2.56kWh of storage and 3.2kW continuous AC output, expandable to 33.28kWh via up to six B500K batteries. It features built-in RV connections, a tilted display, four app-controllable outlets, and Alexa compatibility. BLUETTI positions it as an easier-to-handle alternative to the Apex 300 for buyers wanting portability with room to scale capacity over time.
items.title: BLUETTI Launches Compact Apex 200 Power Station for Homes and RVs

items.summary: Canary Media reports that Democrats won major national and state races in Tuesday's midterm elections, positioning clean energy for gains through new legislative control. The article rounds up results across states: Michigan may pass additional measures after its 2022 trifecta set a target of 100% clean energy by 2040; Minnesota regained House control to advance similar goals; and Wisconsin advocates suggest ending policies that keep polluting plants running while building more solar and batteries. In Georgia, Democrats gained a 3–2 majority on the Public Service Commission for the first time in decades, aided by spending from the Solar Energy Industries Association. Ballot measures also advanced clean energy, including an Oregon tax to fund climate projects. Meanwhile, California's Proposition 45 may be rejected amid mixed support and opposition among developers and environmental groups respectively.
items.title: Clean Energy Gains Follow Democratic Midterm Wins

items.summary: After Democrats routed Republicans Tuesday, analysts say a new era of energy and climate politics begins — one shaped by voters' demand for cheap power rather than decarbonization ambition. New members embraced an 'all of the above' approach, restoring wind and solar tax credits while accepting fossil fuels as status quo. The wave reflects both Trump's failed fossil-fuel agenda and Democrats learning from his mistakes on affordability.
items.title: Democrats’ Energy Moderation Follows Trump’s Climate Reversal

items.summary: Punishing gas prices and a new car affordability crisis are pushing used-car buyers toward electric vehicles, so these used EVs are selling fast across dealer lots. iSeeCars reports the Toyota BZ4x, Lexus RZ300e, Honda Prologue and Polestar 2 average 35 days or less on inventory, with the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron Quattro at just 29.8 days. Meanwhile, used EVs averaged $32,533 in September 2026, up $2,896 from a year earlier.
items.title: High Gas Prices Drive Unprecedented Used EV Demand

items.summary: A report frames Sub-Saharan Africa as a growing natural gas and liquefied natural gas frontier, with buyers shifting away from the Strait of Hormuz. Fitch forecasts SSA’s LNG exports will rise nearly 175% to 98 billion cubic meters by 2034, up from 35.7 bcm in 2024. The African Energy Chamber projects ~$40 billion a year flowing into upstream investment through 2030, lifting hydrocarbon output to 12.5 MMboe/d. Projects are highlighted across Mozambique’s Rovuma Basin, Nigeria’s Train 7 expansion and the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim project in Senegal and Mauritania.
items.title: Africa LNG Exports Projected to Jump as Buyers Avoid Hormuz

items.summary: Voters in this year's midterms signaled strong opposition to data centers, even though the issue was rarely on ballots directly. Candidates who called for limiting development won competitive races in Georgia, Ohio, and Texas; at least 40 local ballot initiatives addressed curbing such projects, with roughly half concentrated in Ohio alone (per Ballotpedia), of which about 24 have been officially approved as results were still being tabulated. Opinion surveys show growing public concern, including overwhelming majorities of Ohioans who said data centers harm the environment and quality of life, and nearly eight in ten favoring a temporary ban on new facilities.
items.title: Midterm Voters Rebuke Data Center Boom

items.summary: Global butane prices are surging, with Northwest European November prices reaching $1,125/t by early November—their highest in 30 years. Asian and US Belvieu prices also hit records at $1,180/t and $920/t respectively. The surge stems from a reorientation of propane/butane trade flows since the March US-Iran war: Gulf exports to Asia collapsed while US share rose to 65%. Seasonal winter blending demand further tightens supplies as American cargoes leave Europe short, with ARA imports falling to 130,000 tonnes. India faced severe LPG shortages after imports dropped from 2.03 million tonnes in February to 1.17 million tonnes in March—a fall of more than 40%. The article notes relief depends on Gulf recovery and maritime security in the Hormuz Strait.
items.title: Butane Prices Hit Decade Highs Amid US Supply Shift

items.summary: At a Wall Street Journal tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday, OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company now earns most of its revenue from enterprise sales and expects to be ready for an initial public offering in 2027. He responded "I think so" when asked about next year's timeline. Reuters reported that San Francisco-based OpenAI has been accelerating fundraising after delaying its IPO plans, while competing with Anthropic over Codex.
items.title: OpenAI President Brockman Signals IPO Readiness for 2027 Amid Enterprise Growth

items.summary: A group of Indian-origin executives now heads major global companies, with Narayen's roughly 19-year tenure since 2007 the longest among them. No official list exists, so counts vary by publication and definition. The most watched transition is at Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy becomes president and CEO on 1 December 2026, succeeding Shantanu Narayen as executive chair. Other recent changes include P&G's Shailesh Jejurikar, Microsoft Gaming's Asha Sharma, and Meta naming Kunal Shah head of WhatsApp alongside a $900 million CRED investment.
items.title: Indian-Origin CEOs Lead Global Firms as Adobe Prepares Leadership Handover

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised the annual coupon on its Floating Rate Bond 2034 to 7.26%, up from 6.45%. An RBI notification dated October 29, 2026 makes the rate applicable from October 30, 2026, until April 29, 2027. For an investment of Rs 1 lakh held at face value, half-yearly interest rises to about Rs 3,630 from Rs 3,225, adding roughly Rs 405 before tax. The coupon resets every six months based on Treasury Bill yields plus a fixed spread, so future payouts may rise or fall.
items.title: RBI Lifts FRB 2034 Coupon, Boosting Half-Yearly Payout

items.summary: Australia's oldest department store chain, David Jones (DJs), has entered voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk amid years of financial struggles as shoppers shift to online shopping. Physical and online stores will keep operating while receivers FTI Consulting review the business. CEO Erica Berthold said it has a plan to reset for the future; receiver Christopher Hill noted rising costs and an outdated footprint drove the decision.
items.title: David Jones enters voluntary administration after nearly two centuries

items.summary: Analysts expect the Bank of England to raise its base rate from 3.75% to 4% on Thursday, marking the first increase in over three years. CPI inflation reached 3.5% in the year to September 2026, up from 3.1%, driven largely by petrol and diesel costs amid the ongoing Iran war impact. The move would raise tracker mortgage repayments for around 510,000 holders while boosting savers.
items.title: Bank of England Rate Hike Anticipated Amid Rising Inflation

items.summary: DBS announced that board director Anthony Lim will become chairman of DBS Group Holdings and DBS Bank on Jan 1, 2027, succeeding Peter Seah. Mr Seah retires after 16 years at the helm following a period of digital transformation and growth. Mr Lim joined the boards in April 2020 and previously spent 19 years at GIC. CEO Tan Su Shan praised both leaders as distinguished bankers who will guide DBS forward.
items.title: DBS Names Anthony Lim Chairman as Peter Seah Retires

items.summary: Voters in Piqua, Trenton and Ashville, Ohio rejected or repealed data center projects tied to Meta, Amazon and EdgeConneX. The local votes joined a national wave of ballot measures against the buildout. Some projects were already underway; Meta had bought more than 600 acres for about $110 million in Piqua last year. Shares of exposed firms fell while hyperscaler stocks rose as traders expected tighter spending.
items.title: Ohio Voters Repeal and Ban Data Center Deals, Pressuring Tech Firms

items.summary: Robert Reich argues that Tuesday's midterm results were not a routine swing against the party in power, but rather an outburst of anti-establishment populism directed at large corporations, mega donors and big tech billionaires. He notes Trump has become part of the establishment he once opposed, while Democrats increasingly campaign on issues like datacenter costs and corporate influence. Reich cites CNBC's late October poll showing corruption as voters' top concern, and quotes newly elected Texas Senate candidate James Talarico saying 'The biggest divide in this country is not left versus right... It's top versus bottom.' He questions whether Democrats will translate the new populism into policy once they control Congress in January. Reich is a former US secretary of labor and Guardian US columnist.
items.title: Robert Reich frames midterms as anti-establishment populist revolt

items.summary: Leander Schaerlaeckens argues that Fifa has met its revenue targets for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn. Per reporting from the Times, about $5bn came from ticket sales and hospitality, which would have made direct fan income five times higher than Qatar's $929m total in 2022. Schaerlaeckens contends Fifa was right only about money matters—dynamic pricing, resales cuts, and cozying up to Donald Trump—while being wrong on fan experience and reforms like mandatory hydration breaks. He concludes the tournament reinforced that real power lies with revenue, leaving little room for reform until the money stream slows.
items.title: Fifa's World Cup Revenue Confirms Its Money-First Priorities

items.summary: The FDA granted tentative approval of a generic lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection that helps prevent HIV infection. The Associated Press reported the drug will cost $40 per person a year in 120 low- and middle-income countries. Approval follows Western aid cuts to African HIV-prevention programs, which sparked fears of hundreds of thousands of additional AIDS deaths. A global health advocate said a large-scale rollout could help bring an end to the HIV epidemic.
items.title: FDA grants tentative approval of low-cost HIV injection

items.summary: Elon Musk spent at least $446m backing Republicans in the US midterm elections, more than his nearly $290m total in 2024. Democrats won every Senate race where America Pac invested heavily and took control of Texas. Talarico said all the money was no match for voters. The spending may end an era of lax regulation benefiting Musk's companies as Democratic officials vow scrutiny.
items.title: Musk's Record Midterm Spending Backed by Democratic Gains

items.summary: Canada-US Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said Wednesday that Ottawa will continue trade negotiations with the Trump administration after the November 5, 2026 midterms. He noted the new Congress takes office in January and that talks are handled by the executive branch. LeBlanc stressed Canada's focus on affordability, major projects, economic strengthening and diversifying trade relationships remains unchanged.
items.title: Canada Presses Trade Talks After US Midterms

items.summary: Guardian Australia reports that Beau Lamarre-Condon, a 31-year-old police officer accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his service weapon at their Paddington home on 19 February 2024, gave testimony during the high-profile Sydney trial. He told the court he was transferred to the youth command division to escape officers tormenting him at Surry Hills station, described remembering 12 to 15 graphic incidents as an officer, and recounted a co-worker who shot himself in the head while off duty.
items.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon gives evidence in double murder trial

items.summary: Sources said Wednesday that Mitsui Chemicals is considering acquiring semiconductor materials maker JSR in a possible deal worth over ¥1 trillion, which could become Japan’s largest chemical-industry acquisition. The company stated it is examining options to improve corporate value and strengthen its semiconductor business. Shares would be bought from parent fund Japan Investment Corporation (JIC), which took JSR private for about ¥900 billion in 2024.
items.title: Mitsui Chemicals Weighs Over ¥1 Trillion Bid for JSR

items.summary: On Wednesday, Hungary released communist-era secret police files identifying tens of thousands of former informants in a long-delayed reckoning with the country's repressive past. The move was spearheaded by Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who ousted Viktor Orban in April on a promise of regime change and pressed ahead with a bill granting unrestricted public access to the records for the first time.
items.title: Hungary Releases Communist-Era Informer Files Under Magyar Government

items.summary: Australian frozen yoghurt chain Yo-Chi is opening its newest outlet at i12 Katong on Thursday (Nov 5) at 11am. The launch features a collaboration with heritage bakery Chin Mee Chin, offering two limited-edition toppings—the Kaya Swiss Roll and the kaya-filled Choux Puff—for three days only. A new Iced Latte yoghurt flavour is also introduced.
items.title: Yo-Chi Opens Katong Outlet With Chin Mee Chin Toppings and New Iced Latte Yoghurt

items.summary: South Korea's defence ministry announced Thursday it would deploy maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive ordnance disposal team near the Strait of Hormuz to help keep the waterway open. The mission, which will include a destroyer and unmanned vessels, is strictly for non-combat purposes and operates independently of allied forces. Seoul maintains it will not intervene militarily in the US-Iran war that began February 28.
items.title: South Korea Deploys Non-Combat Mission Near Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The remains of Jenny Balcarras and her daughter Selah Reed were found after their family reported them missing on Sunday. Investigators say multiple grizzly bears could have been involved in the attack, which killed both women in British Columbia. They are continuing to search for the bears, which will be killed for public safety.
items.title: Investigators probe deadly grizzly bear attack in British Columbia

items.summary: The Guardian enlisted a team of critics to review the six books on the Booker Prize 2026 shortlist, which pits literary heavyweights against first-time nominees. The judging panel, led by classicist Mary Beard and including poet Raymond Antrobus, musician Jarvis Cocker, editor Rebecca Liu, and novelist Patricia Lockwood, settled its choice after reading 163 books in seven months. The list includes two past winners—Marlon James and Douglas Stuart—as well as debut novels from Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, plus genre fiction by M John Harrison. The review covers each title's premise, tone, and themes before noting the £50,000 ($95,000) prize will be awarded in London on November 9 (November 10 in Australia).
items.title: Critics review six Booker Prize 2026 shortlisted novels

items.summary: Tiger mosquitoes, once confined to tropical regions, are now established across several European countries and moving north roughly 60 kilometres a year. Health authorities warn the diseases they carry — dengue, chikungunya and Zika — could follow. By end of October 2026, Italy reported 76 locally acquired dengue cases and France eight, about twice the previous year's totals. Portugal released 30,000 sterile male mosquitoes in a second attempt to curb populations. Experts stress that elimination is unrealistic; instead they emphasize surveillance, community engagement and preparing diagnostics — with HERA funding €10 million for new tools.
items.title: Europe Races to Contain Spreading Tiger Mosquitoes and Tropical Diseases

items.summary: The US State Department designated two individuals and one entity accused of helping Iran obtain man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). The targets are Mohammed Ali Tolibov, CEO of Belarus-based Armory Alliance; Nigeria-based Vanguard Tactical Supply Limited; and Russia-based Alisher Domullodzhanov. Officials allege the network sought to procure Chinese-origin MANPADS for Iran using false end-users.
items.title: US Sanctions Three Over Alleged Iran MANPADS Supply Efforts

items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term on 25 October 2026, taking 51.79% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.21%. Three weeks earlier, however, Flávio led the first round with 47.03% versus Lula’s 45.16%, a result that prompted widespread mobilization behind “from mourning to struggle.” The article attributes Lula’s comeback to collective street and digital organizing rather than any single strategy or announcement. It also flags structural challenges: an August–September survey found 82% of families in debt, the benchmark interest rate stood at 13.75%, and markets may resist continued social spending.
items.title: Lula’s Narrow Runoff Victory Reveals Brazil’s Far-Right Resilience

items.summary: World leaders gathered in Madrid for the 30th Ibero-American Summit, inaugurated by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia at the Teatro Real. Although Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez welcomed delegations from the 22-member community, only 10 countries were represented by their heads of state or government. The absence of Brazil's Lula da Silva, Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum and Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez highlighted political divisions ahead of Spain's general election on 29 November.
items.title: Madrid Opens Ibero-American Summit Amid Low Attendance

items.summary: South Sudan hosts the world’s biggest mammal migration, roughly 6 million antelopes moving across seasonal swamps and grassland. A new GPS tracking map joins millions of collar data points from 262 migratory animals recorded since 2023 to reveal these “lines of life.” The routes span four species — white-eared kob, tiang, Mongalla gazelle and bohor reedbuck — mostly outside Boma and Badingilo national parks. A 2025 aerial survey estimates populations around 5.17 million kob, with no growth or decline since 2023. Conservationists say the map helps target protection of high-use areas amid rising commercial hunting.
items.title: GPS map charts South Sudan’s largest antelope migration outside its parks

items.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) flagged four high-severity vulnerabilities across select versions of Tata Motors’ iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, which could expose credentials or enable user impersonation. Impacted apps are those at version 26.7.3 or below for iRA 2.0 and 26.7.2 or below for iRA.ev. CERT-In advised users to upgrade to the latest versions, though an email sent to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles went unanswered.
items.title: CERT-In Flags High-Severity Vulnerabilities in Tata Motors iRA Connected Vehicle Apps

items.summary: Alphabet's Google confirmed to Reuters that it began offering voluntary exit packages in June, expanding the program globally across Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland. The move comes amid rising artificial intelligence spending that has pressured Alphabet's stock price. A spokesperson said some teams introduced a voluntary exit program with severance this year.
items.title: Google Expands Voluntary Exit Offers Across Five Countries Amid AI Spending

items.summary: The government relaxed key terms in its effort to procure 10,000 fresh GPUs under the IndiaAI Mission. Providers can now qualify with a minimum capacity of 512 GPUs or TPUs at one Indian data centre location, down from 1,000 earlier. The first stage covers technical qualification only; bidders need not submit a financial bid or commit to service levels. The minimum qualifying score fell to 60 out of 100 from 75 under the prior framework.
items.title: IndiaAI GPU procurement eases entry, price pain persists

items.summary: After the Nifty and Sensex fell about 8% each in Samvat 2082, ET compiled 15 stock ideas from five brokerages that analysts believe are well placed to outperform in Samvat 2083. The picks reflect analyst views rather than verified forecasts.
items.title: Economic Times lists 15 stocks poised for Samvat 2083 rebound

items.summary: Ravi Uppal, a prime accused in the multi-crore Mahadev online betting case, was arrested by Dubai police. Enforcement authorities have formally moved for his extradition and sources say he is likely to be handed over soon. India had requested his return after learning of the arrest; agencies again located him in May this year. Uppal helped launch the app in 2019 and franchised thousands of branches on a profit-sharing basis.
items.title: India Seeks Extradition of Mahadev Betting Accused Held in Dubai

items.summary: Around 10 State Disaster Response Force personnel were feared missing after two boats allegedly capsized during a rescue operation to save stranded fishermen at Bethupalli lake in Khammam district, Telangana, on Wednesday evening. The incident occurred amid heavy rainfall from cyclone Murasu. Revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said teams had identified the possible location of the missing personnel and that they would be rescued safely, while Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar confirmed NDRF deployment and ongoing search efforts as officials continued rescue operations.
items.title: Telangana Officials Search for SDRF Personnel After Boats Capsize

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, eight stocks in the Nifty200 pack had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on November 4, 2026. Traders use the 200-day DMA as a key indicator of overall trend; when a stock stays above it on the daily timeframe, it is generally read as being in an uptrend.
items.title: Eight Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: ENIL posted consolidated revenue of ₹117 crore for the quarter, including domestic revenue of ₹114 crore. The company said its Ebitda loss in the digital business narrowed to ₹7.5 crore from ₹9.8 crore a year earlier. ENIL remains focused on growing Gaana's subscriber base through partnerships.
items.title: ENIL Reports Q2 Ebitda Rise on Cost Cuts and Lower Digital Losses

items.summary: The US Treasury Department on Wednesday imposed fresh sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over alleged support for Iran, Reuters reported. The action is part of the Trump administration's 'Operation Economic Outcast', aimed at restricting Iran's oil-export revenue. It targets an India-based network allegedly providing fraudulent maritime flags to vessels carrying Iranian petroleum, including Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid and nine linked entities. Separately, Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc was designated for supporting Iran's aviation sector. The Treasury said earlier sanctions had contributed to a sharp decline in the rial and domestic inflation approaching 90%. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would keep targeting those facilitating support for Tehran by land, sea or air. "We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime," he said.
items.title: US Sanctions Indian Entities Over Iran Oil and Aviation Support

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a high alert for heavy rains across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh on November 5 as Cyclone Murasu dissipated. For Delhi-NCR it forecast shallow morning fog with maximum temperatures around 27°C to 29°C and minimums of 15°C to 17°C, both below normal. The Central Pollution Control Board reported the AQI at 368 in 'very poor' conditions on Thursday morning, with Punjabi Bagh reaching 458 in the 'severe' category.
items.title: IMD Warns of Heavy Rains in South; Delhi Air Quality Stays Poor

items.summary: Finshots explains why India has not expanded its emergency oil reserves despite importing nearly 90% of crude and facing calls from former RBI governor C. Rangarajan to stockpile more. The country's ISPRL-managed strategic reserve holds about 5.33 million tonnes, roughly a week of imports at current inventory levels. Expansion (Phase II) is stalled by cost—building facilities could run ₹15,000 crore and filling them over ₹25,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore—and delays in construction. Suggested fixes include buying crude when prices are low, a revolving fund, and joint stockpiling with producers like ADNOC.
items.title: Why India Has Not Built Bigger Emergency Oil Reserves

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attacked Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann over his anti-drug record, alleging he smelled of alcohol during a parliamentary sitting around 11 am. Speaking at the Congress Insaaf Rally in Sangrur on November 4, Gandhi questioned whether Mann could fight drug abuse while consuming it regularly and challenged the AAP's promise to eradicate drugs from Punjab. The remarks intensified the Congress-AAP contest ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections despite both parties being INDIA bloc allies nationally. The Aam Aadmi Party responded by calling the rally 'directionless' and accusing Congress of electoral decline.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi's alcohol remark at Bhagwant Mann sparks AAP rebuttal ahead of Punjab polls

items.summary: The Delhi Police transferred Inspector Arun Kumar on Wednesday, a day after suspending Assistant Commissioner of Police Manasvi Vashisht following a protest by over 100 police personnel outside the headquarters. The officers demanded reinstatement and to present their version of an October 23 incident at Shahdara station that left advocate Lalit Bansal injured. Kumar was moved again to the Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations Branch, per an order from the Delhi Police Commissioner's office.
items.title: Delhi Police Inspector Transferred Again After ACP Suspension

items.summary: Kerala Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan said former governor Rajendra Arlekar did not consult the state government before recommending to President Droupadi Murmu the removal of Public Service Commission chairman MR Baiju after irregularities in recruitment exams surfaced. This was the first such recommendation by a Kerala governor, and the Crime Branch is probing the matter.
items.title: Satheesan says ex-governor bypassed state on PSC chief removal

items.summary: Democrats won sweeping majorities in both chambers of Congress after the US midterm elections, setting up a confrontation with President Donald Trump over his legislative agenda. Though they gained room to advance bills, Democrats remain short of the two-thirds majority needed to override vetoes. Trump has signalled he may use veto power and the unoverridable pocket veto to block legislation, while also threatening bills before passage via Statements of Administration Policy.
items.title: Trump's Veto Powers After Democratic Midterm Gains

items.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), through its National Cybercrime Threat Analysis Unit in coordination with CERT-In, issued an advisory on November 3, 2026 warning banks, NBFCs and fintech firms of a rising threat from AI-assisted cyberattacks targeting payment APIs. The advisory explains that criminals exploit unpatched software, misconfigured servers and agentic AI to move multi-crore funds at machine speed through mule accounts before deleting records. It urges stronger API security, transaction monitoring and beneficiary verification, and reiterates the six-hour incident-reporting rule to CERT-In and RBI's DAKSH portal.
items.title: I4C Alerts Financial Firms to AI-Powered Payment API Attacks

items.summary: Brent crude and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell below the $100-per-barrel threshold on Thursday, reaching their lowest levels in over two months amid reactions to the US midterm elections. Brent slipped below $95 while WTI dropped under $90 as markets weighed expectations that a Democratic congressional majority could pressure President Donald Trump toward a negotiated settlement with Iran. Oil inventories also fell 865,000 barrels last week.
items.title: Crude oil prices fall below $100 after US midterm elections

items.summary: About 10 State Disaster Response Force personnel were feared missing after their boats were suspected to have capsized while rescuing fishermen stranded in Bethupalli lake in Khammam district of Telangana on Wednesday evening, official sources said. The operation took place amid heavy rains under cyclone 'Murasu'. Officials and NDRF teams rushed to rescue the personnel.
items.title: Ten SDRF Personnel Feared Missing After Boats Capsize in Telangana

items.summary: Transport Minister A. Vijay Thamizhan Parthiban announced that TNSTC would run a total of 15,659 buses including 9.086 special buses from November 5 to 7 to meet the passenger demand during the Deepavali celebrations. Services in the return direction numbered 11,967 including 6,815 special buses on November 9 and 10.
items.title: Tamil Nadu minister announces extra buses for Deepavali travel rush

items.summary: The family of slain Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar has approached the Bombay High Court, alleging that the Special Investigation Team probing his September 29 murder failed to make meaningful progress and seeking a court-monitored transfer to an independent agency. The plea cites lapses over evidence, suspects and eyewitness confidentiality, notes five arrests so far after 35 days, and references Uttar Pradesh STF material allegedly suppressed by investigators. Thane Police Commissioner Ashutosh Dumbare maintains the probe is progressing correctly; all allegations remain unexamined by the court.
items.title: Purnekar Family Petitions Bombay High Court Over SIT Probe Lapses

items.summary: The piece reflects on Diwali, noting that while homes are cleaned and streets lit each year, many hearts remain restless despite the display of light. It frames the festival's tradition around inner illumination rather than material celebration, citing examples like Shri Ram's return to Ayodhya and Mahavira's enlightenment as symbols of spiritual renewal. The author urges readers to pause before lighting decorative lamps and instead reflect on awakening their own awareness.
items.title: Diwali as a Call for Inner Spiritual Renewal

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Madhya Pradesh Assembly Speaker to decide within two months a disqualification plea against rebel Congress MLA Nirmala Sapre under the anti-defection law, which had been pending for over two years. The petition was filed in July 2024 by Leader of Opposition Umang Singhar, who alleges that Sapre abandoned her Congress membership and joined the BJP after winning on a Congress ticket in 2023. Sapre has denied resigning from Congress or joining the BJP.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Speaker To Rule On Disqualification Plea Within Two Months
